cards.title: Performance Comparison and Species Count Necessity
cards.claim: Testing on 26 Wyeth compounds showed that the new rat, dog, monkey, rat-dog, and rat-monkey methods provided improved predictions for the majority of compounds compared to the Rule of Exponents (ROE). This suggests that using three or more species in an allometrically based approach may not be necessary for predicting human exposure.
conditions: Based on a validation set of 26 compounds.
Focus is on clearance prediction accuracy.
required_inputs: Validation dataset of compounds with animal and human CL data.
limitations: Abstract does not specify the statistical metrics of 'improved predictions' (e.g., AAFE, bias).
Generalizability to other drug classes beyond the Wyeth dataset is unknown.
cards.downstream_use: Supports the feasibility of using limited species data (1 or 2 species) for human PK prediction, challenging the necessity of multi-species datasets for all cases.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
